audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Gnar levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items, but its own whys say the opposite at 2, 3 and first item ('he chips you for free', 'he keeps the edge kiting', 'his first lethality item... out-scale your bridge item'). Gnar also loses this lane at 48.37%.
audit.why: Avengerang (850 range, 9/8/7/6/5s) plus his auto range beat a walk-up 1100-range Boomerang because Gnar must step in to throw; Heroic Swing (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s) removes him from the counter-trade.
audit.corrected: Levels 2, 3 and first item -> Akshan. Result matches the packet chart exactly: Skill, Akshan, Akshan, Skill, Skill, Akshan, Gnar.

audit.why: Spike order is right: Akshan at 2-3 on range, Gnar at the first full Rage bar and again at 6 with GNAR! into terrain, Akshan again on his first lethality item. Gnar's spikes are Rage-driven, not level-driven, and the text already says so.
audit.corrected: Kept; first-item spike now names Going Rogue and the vision requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never named a single Akshan ability (packet defect), and neither layer mentioned Dirty Fighting's shield or that Going Rogue is camouflage you cannot reveal.
audit.why: Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit from attacks and abilities against a champion, so a Mega burst opened cold is partly eaten. Going Rogue carries the stealth flag and Gnar has no reveal in his kit — Control Wards and a sweeper are the only answer, which matters most around shoves and roams.
audit.corrected: Avengerang, Heroic Swing (with cooldowns), Going Rogue and Dirty Fighting named in the content layer and in the do's; shield-before-burst and ward-before-shove stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] told the player to stick to Akshan 'while he's grounded'. Nothing in Gnar's kit grounds, and nothing in Akshan's kit grounds him.
audit.why: Gnar's tools are a slow (Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss), a stun (Wallop), a dash (Hop) and GNAR!'s displacement — no grounding. The claim would tell a player Heroic Swing is disabled when it is not.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real condition: close while Heroic Swing's 18s cooldown is down.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] and dontsFull[1] carry inherited boilerplate details that do not match their own titles.
audit.why: 'Manage rage for Mega on demand' was paired with text about Akshan wasting Heroic Swing; 'Hop into his engage' was paired with generic cooldown-waste text.
audit.corrected: Both details rewritten with the real mechanic and number (Dirty Fighting's third-hit shield; Hop's 22s at rank 1).

edits.before: Rage management is the champion — track your own bar. Only take the trade when Akshan's Heroic Swing is down.
edits.after: Avengerang out-ranges your walk-up Boomerang at 2 — last-hit at max range and wait for the Rage bar to fill.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Akshan must walk into your range.
edits.after: He kites with Avengerang and leaves on Heroic Swing (18s) — Mini has no answer, so farm and hold the wave your side.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Heroic Swing's cooldown.
edits.after: His lethality spike out-paces yours — ward before you shove and play for the wall-ult pick.

edits.before: His level-2 Q and auto range out-distance your walk-up Boomerang, so he chips you for free every time you step into Mini range.
edits.after: Avengerang (Q, 9s at rank 1) and his auto range out-distance your walk-up Boomerang, so he chips you free every time you step in.

edits.before: He keeps the edge kiting with Q poke and E-grapple mobility while your Mini form has no answer and Rage is not yet reliable.
edits.after: He keeps the edge kiting with Avengerang poke and Heroic Swing mobility while your Mini form has no answer and Rage is unreliable.

edits.before: Akshan's Q and auto range out-distance your Mini Boomerang, so he chips you every time you walk up to throw Q — and his E grapple lets him swing off to safety before you can answer.
edits.after: Avengerang and his auto range out-distance your Mini Boomerang, so he chips you every time you walk up to throw — and Heroic Swing (18s) takes him to safety before you can answer.

edits.before: His lethality item plus passive camo lets him roam off cooldown and punish your shove far harder than your bridge/tank item helps you stick to him.
edits.after: His lethality item plus Going Rogue camouflage lets him roam and punish your shove harder than your item helps you stick — Control Ward before you push.

edits.before: Bait the return Boomerang catch to refund Q, then chain Mini W's third-hit move speed to stick on him while he's grounded
edits.after: Catch the returning Boomerang to refund its cooldown, then chain Hyper's third-hit move speed to close while Heroic Swing is down

edits.before: Akshan wastes Heroic Swing — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Dirty Fighting shields every third hit — force it, then transform.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Hop is 22s at rank 1 — spend it leaving his range, never entering it.

notes: Level-chart flips are proposed as one group across both layers and land exactly on the packet's chart. I did not claim Going Rogue is a general lane escape: Riot's text ties the camouflage to moving toward Scoundrels, so it is written as a roaming/vision problem, not an in-lane disengage. Nothing asserted about Rage fill rate — Riot's data gives no number.
